# github

```go
import "github.com/blanketops/environments-bots/internal/github"
```

Package github is the small part of the GitHub REST and GraphQL APIs that test\-helper uses: issues, labels, comments and Projects \(v2\) items. It authenticates with the token the calling workflow passes in, normally an installation token of the BlanketOps\-Environments App.

<a name="Client.AddLabels"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) AddLabels

```go
func (c *Client) AddLabels(ctx context.Context, number int, labels []string) error
```

AddLabels adds labels to an issue or pull request \(pull requests are labelled through the issues API\). Adding a label that is already there is a no\-op, so this is safe to repeat.

<a name="Client.CreateBranch"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) CreateBranch

```go
func (c *Client) CreateBranch(ctx context.Context, branch, sha string) error
```

CreateBranch creates branch at commit sha. No commit is made, so the branch carries only commits that already exist.

<a name="Client.CreateCommitOnBranch"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) CreateCommitOnBranch

```go
func (c *Client) CreateCommitOnBranch(ctx context.Context, branch, headline, body, expectedHead string, additions []FileAddition, deletions []string) (string, error)
```

CreateCommitOnBranch makes a commit on branch with the given file additions and deletions through the GraphQL createCommitOnBranch mutation, and returns the new commit's OID. A commit made this way with an App installation token is signed by GitHub and shows as verified — a git commit in a workflow is not, so a branch requiring verified signatures refuses it. expectedHead is the commit the branch must still point at, so a racing update fails the mutation instead of being clobbered.


<a name="Client.Merge"></a>
### func \(\*Client\) Merge

```go
func (c *Client) Merge(ctx context.Context, base, head, message string) (string, error)
```

Merge merges head into base with a server\-side merge commit and returns the merge commit's SHA. GitHub signs the commit, so it satisfies the branch's required\-signatures rule without a ruleset bypass. The SHA is empty when base already contains head \(HTTP 204, nothing to merge\). IsConflict\(err\) reports a merge conflict \(HTTP 409\); the caller resolves it, as a bot cannot.

<a name="Commit"></a>
## type Commit

Commit is a commit's SHA, full message and number of parents \(more than one for a merge commit, whatever its message says\).

```go
type Commit struct {
    SHA     string
    Message string
    Parents int
}
```


<a name="Issue"></a>
## type Issue

Issue is a repository issue.

```go
type Issue struct {
    Number  int    `json:"number"`
    Title   string `json:"title"`
    State   string `json:"state"`
    NodeID  string `json:"node_id"`
    HTMLURL string `json:"html_url"`
    // PullRequest is set when the "issue" is a pull request; the issues
    // API lists both.
    PullRequest *struct{} `json:"pull_request,omitempty"`
    // User is the issue's author.
    User struct {
        Login string `json:"login"`
    }   `json:"user"`
}
```

<a name="PullDetail"></a>
## type PullDetail

PullDetail is one pull request's detail \(GET /pulls/\{number\}\): its head and base branches and, once merged, whether it merged and the merge commit.

```go
type PullDetail struct {
    Number         int
    Title          string

    Head           string

}
```

<a name="PullFile"></a>
## type PullFile

PullFile is one file changed in a pull request \(GET /pulls/\{number\}/files\).

```go
type PullFile struct {
```
